plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your value, resulting in zero profit. Bidding above your value risks winning but paying more than the item is worth to you. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately 2/3 * 20 = $13.33. To maximize profit and win, I should bid just above this. However, my value is $23, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid $13.40 to ensure I win against bids below that.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the item when it's worth more to you, and any bid above your value risks overpaying. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid my true value of $11.
